build_to.study_cross_check_note: The study's own 1647 mm2 / 38.8 g cross-check is arithmetically wrong and the model is right. Recomputing the same outline analytically from the same four numbers (48.5 tip radius, 11 arm, 11 hub, 40 deg tip, 8 hole) gives a taper 15.1111 mm long starting at 33.3889 mm and an area of 1668.42 mm2, i.e. 39.29 g at 3.0 mm before any bevel. SHURIKEN_STUDY.md 2.1 should read 1668 mm2 / 39.3 g. References/ is read-only for this build, so the correction is recorded here instead; it is worth making before the other seven variants reuse the pattern.

lod1_is_distinct.note: Rev 1's LOD1 reproduced LOD0 to nine significant figures because LOD0's extra triangles were a coplanar 64-spoke hub fan that Decimate removed for free. That fan is gone: LOD0's budget now goes on the three-segment rounded ground bevel. What remains is inherent, not padding - a flat plate whose bevel is a ruled surface swept along a straight taper can be collapsed lengthwise almost free, so any LOD0 that meets study 4's 1,200 triangle floor will be reducible with small surface error. The deviation figure above is the honest measure: max distance from an LOD0 vertex to the LOD1 surface.

originality.basis: historical juji / shiho hira-shuriken, public domain (study 5)
originality.tip_taper: 40.0 deg included, ground over the last 15.1 mm, ending in a 1.20 mm chisel edge
originality.finish: blackened oxide, not flat grey: base colour (0.035, 0.034, 0.033) linear with bare steel worn through on the points and the ground bevels
originality.stamp: none (study 5 allows no stamp on the first piece; any future mark must be an invented glyph)
originality.franchise_strings: none in any object, mesh, material, texture or file name; qa_check no_franchise_strings passed on every object

fixes_applied: BLOCKER topology: the 16 coincident vertices / 16 zero-length edges / 32 zero-area triangles the clamped bmesh bevel left at every bevel run-out are gone. The plate, bevel included, is authored explicitly through a 1 nm position-keyed vertex factory, so a duplicate vertex cannot be created, and every face loop drops repeated indices so a collapsed quad becomes a triangle instead of a sliver. The build refuses to save unless zero-length edges, zero-area faces and coincident vertices are all zero.

BLOCKER qa gate: Scripts/pipeline/qa_check.py gained no_zero_length_edges, no_degenerate_faces and no_coincident_vertices, and test_qa_negative.py case 12 reproduces the exact defect and proves those three checks - and only those three - fire on it. The gate is now 55 checks on this asset, not 46.

MAJOR bevel: 0.9 mm requested, 0.9 mm measured on the finished mesh (rev 1 shipped 0.323 mm and reported 0.9). No operator clamp is involved any more; the achieved value is measured from the mesh and recorded, not copied from the request.

MAJOR topology / budget: the 64-spoke hub fan is gone. The hub ring is 32 segments bridged 2:1 to a 16-segment hole ring, the arm is 4 columns across instead of 9, and each tip caps in a 4-triangle fan. The budget now buys a 3-segment rounded ground bevel over the taper - real 3D detail - rather than coplanar filler.

MAJOR LOD screen sizes: pipeline.export_fbx now writes lod_screen_sizes (study 4's 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25) into the .sockets.json sidecar, and pipeline.ue_import_sockets applies them with StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.set_lod_screen_sizes after import, so Unreal stops inventing 2.0 / 0.75 / 0.5625 and parking the star on LOD2.

BLOCKER renders: the preview rig was rebuilt around a real ground plane with a contact shadow, a structured dark environment and grazing strip lights. The product now measures the same value in the hero and the spec shot instead of 3.2x apart, the 0.9 mm ground facet catches a highlight, the rim wall reads as steel rather than an ink outline, and the top view is lit with 4-fold symmetry.

MAJOR material: M_Shuriken_Master gained the wear story study 3 specifies - bright bare steel on the points and the ground bevels over a blackened coating - plus a directional radial grind instead of isotropic mottling. Base colour lifted from (0.018, 0.018, 0.021) to (0.035, 0.034, 0.033): dark, neutral, and off pure black.

MINOR centre hole: the hole polygon is circumscribed, so the minimum opening is a true 8.000 mm across the flats (rev 1's inscribed 16-gon measured 8 mm across the corners and only 7.846 mm across the flats, so an 8 mm pin would not pass).
MINOR framing: gallery images are 16:9 so they survive the Fab 1920x1080 thumbnail crop (study 7) instead of losing the tips, and a LOD strip was added.

MINOR report accuracy: texel density, the tip description and the Grip socket axis are all measured from the file now. The socket's Blender local +X points radially INWARD by design - make_socket bakes the documented 180 deg Y correction - and the sidecar's Unreal yaw is what matters; rev 1's report described this as a defect.

known_gaps: LOD1 still reproduces LOD0's surface closely: max deviation 1e-06 mm for a 55% triangle saving. The cause named in review - a coplanar 64-spoke hub fan padding LOD0 - is fixed, but the residue is inherent: this plate's bevel is a ruled surface swept along a straight taper, so Decimate can collapse it lengthwise at almost no geometric cost. Any LOD0 that meets study 4's 1,200-triangle floor on this silhouette will be reducible the same way. Hand-authoring LOD1 at a lower density would fix it, but the task and ASSET_GUIDELINES 6.2 mandate decimate_lods; raising the question against the study's floor is the real fix and belongs to whoever owns References/.

LOD1 and LOD2 vertex sets are not C4 as point sets (only their surfaces are), because Decimate re-triangulates the coplanar interior asymmetrically. LOD0 is now exactly C4: the 90 deg rotation test gives a 0.000000 mm deviation, because the four quarters are generated with integer quarter-turns and snapped positions rather than a rotation matrix. Any C4 gate added to qa_check must test the silhouette, not the vertex set.

UV coverage is 31.7% of the square. Sweeping the packer over 20 shape_method x margin_method x margin combinations moved it only between 26.0% and 32.0%, so the packer is not the limit - Smart UV Project's island shapes are. Hand-laying the shells belongs to the pack-atlas pass, where the budget is shared across eight variants, not to one star.

SHURIKEN_STUDY.md 2.1's cross-check (1647 mm2 / 38.8 g) is arithmetically wrong; see build_to.study_cross_check_note. References/ is read-only for this build, so it is recorded rather than corrected. Worth fixing before the other seven variants reuse the pattern.

No texture bake (out of scope for the first piece). The wear and grind are procedural and Cycles-only: they carry the renders, and the FBX exports only the Principled scalars, so nothing about them reaches the engine.

The imported material slot binds to WorldGridMaterial because the verification import runs with import_materials=False. The slot NAME survives the FBX, so slot-based assignment works. Whether the pack ships a UE material asset or documents that the buyer assigns their own is a listing decision, not a mesh defect.

LightMapResolution is left at Unreal's default 64 for a 9.7 cm prop, and the generated UV1 has never been exercised because the validation project sets r.AllowStaticLighting=False. Dropping it to 16 or 32 and doing one build-lighting pass belongs to the Unreal-side import settings, not to this build script.

The round hub still does not read strongly at gallery size - the arm base corners sit at radius 11.02 mm against an 11.00 mm hub, so only small arcs of hub are exposed. That is what the reference outline draws and the hub radius is load-bearing for the area and the mass, so no geometry was changed; the ring lighting gives it what value break it can. Worth a line in the listing copy rather than a mesh edit.
